latest_rss.title: Sensitive Words: Search Censorship, Tiananmen, “8 Squared,” and “64 + Division”
latest_rss.summary:
Ahead of the 37th anniversary of the June Fourth crackdown, CDT Chinese editors compiled a number of related terms subject to search censorship across various Chinese online platforms. The terms, detected by a Citizen Lab tracking system, are just a few examples of the long-evolving efforts to "clear the online square" each year. 
Direct references:

六四 liùsì, "64" in Chinese characters  
六4 liù4, "64" in a mix of Chinese and Arabic numerals  
6肆 6sì, another mix using an anti-fraud character for "4"  
陆肆 lùsì, 64 in anti-fraud characters  
8 de + píngfāng, "8 squared"  
535 + 64. “535” refers to “May 35th,” a coded reference to June 4th that is now itself targeted for censorship  
64 + 29 nián, "64 + 29 years," likely carried over from 2018
